name: Jeshua
overview: Jeshua is a male Levite known primarily as the son of Azaniah, as recorded in Nehemiah 10:9. Unlike some Levites who served as priests, Jeshua is distinguished as a Levite rather than a priest. He is listed among the signatories of the sealed covenant document in Nehemiah 10:1-27, marking his role in the post-exilic community's commitment to God's law.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeshua means 'YHWH saves,' reflecting the saving nature of God. This proper name is noted in Nehemiah 10:9 and was not given directly by God but carries significant theological meaning consistent with God's redemptive character.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Jeshua as the son of Azaniah in Nehemiah 10:9. No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jeshua's significance lies in his role as a Levite participant in the covenant renewal documented in Nehemiah 10. His inclusion among the signatories highlights his commitment to the community's spiritual restoration and adherence to God's commands after the exile. Being a Levite rather than a priest, Jeshua represents the faithful service of the Levitical tribe in maintaining the religious life of Israel during this critical period.
